p: two days was the feast of: By the will of God, against the counsel of men, it came to pass that Christ should be put to death upon the solemn day of the passover, that in all respects the truth of his sacrifice might agree to the symbol of the passover.
And there were some that had: Rash judgments are made void before God.
three hundred pence: Which is about six English pounds.
For ye have the poor with: Christ allowed himself to be anointed once or twice for certain considerations: but his will is to be daily anointed in the poor.
She hath done what she could: This woman, by the secret influence of the Spirit, anoints Christ, and thus sets before men's eyes his death and burial which were at hand.
And Judas Iscariot: Covetousness disguised with a zeal of charity is an occasion to betray and crucify Christ.

And the first day of unleavened: Christ being made subject to the law for us celebrates the passover according to the law: and in addition by a miracle shows that even though he will immediately suffer in the flesh, that he is yet God.
when: That is, upon this day, and at the evening of the same day, which was the beginning of the fifteenth. See Geneva
they killed the: They used to sacrifice.
passover: That is, spoken thus, by the figure of speech called metonymy, which is commonly used when talking about sacraments, and by the passover is meant the paschal lamb.

upper room furnished and prepared: The Greek word signifies that part of the house that is highest from the ground, and because they used to eat supper in that part of the house they called it a supper room, no matter what they were using it for.

And as they sat and did: The types in the law, which are to be fulfilled before long, are cancelled: and in place of them are put symbols of the new covenant corresponding to them, which will continue to the world's end.
dippeth with me in the dish: That regularly eats with me.
And Jesus saith unto them: Christ foretells how he will be forsaken by his own, but yet that he will never forsake them.
But Peter said unto him: Here is set forth in an excellent person a most sorrowful example of man's rashness and weakness.
more vehemently: The doubling of words here sets out more plainly Peter's vehement affirmation.

Christ suffering for us the most horrible terrors of the curse of God, in that flesh which he took upon him for our sakes, receives the cup from his Father's hands, which he being just, drinks right away for the unjust.
Abba: This doubling of the word was used in those days when their languages were mixed together: for the word "Abba" is a Syrian word.
And he cometh: A horrible example of the sluggishness of men, even among the disciples whom Christ had chosen.

And immediately: As men willingly robbed God their creator of his praise in forsaking and betraying him: so Christ, willingly going about to make satisfaction for this ruin, is forsaken by his own, and betrayed by one of his familiar acquaintances as a thief, so that the punishment might be in agreement with the sin, and that we who are ourselves traitors, forsakers and those committing sacrilege, might be delivered out of the devil's snare.
safely: So diligently that he cannot escape out of your hand.
one of them that stood by: That is, Peter.
all forsook him: All his disciples.
And there followed him a certain: Under a pretence of godliness, all things are lawful to those who do violence against Christ.

linen cloth cast about his naked: Which he cast about him, and ran forth after he heard the commotion in the night: by this we may understand with how great licentiousness these villains violently set upon him.

assembled all the chief priests and: The highest council was assembled because Christ was accused as a blasphemer and a false prophet: for as to the other crime of treason, it was forged against him by the priest in order to force Pilate to condemn him.

And the chief priests and all: Christ, who was so innocent that he could not be oppressed, not even by false witnesses, is at length condemned for impiety before the high priest for confessing God to be his father. This is so that we, who denied God and were indeed wicked, might be acquitted before God.
Blessed: Of God, who is most worthy of all praise?
And some began to spit on: Christ, suffering all types of reproach for our sakes, gets everlasting glory for those that believe in him.
And as Peter was beneath in: A grievous example of the frailness of man together with a most comfortable example of the mercy of God, who gives the spirit of repentance and faith to his elect.

a maid saw him again: If we carefully compare the evangelists together we will perceive that Peter was known by many through the maiden's report: furthermore, when the second denial is spoken of in Luke, there is a man servant mentioned and not a maid.
